decisions.what: Who reads the document, and which names does it give Turn's things?
decisions.decided: A developer, a person or an AI, who builds or changes Turn. The document keeps the UX's and the README's names: the person, the calling AI, a work, its kind, a point, the design, a best practice, the generator, the evaluator. It adds, each defined where first used: up, the subagent turn:up that starts Turn's roles and carries each point; the starter, whoever starts up, the main conversation by the steps of /turn:up or the calling AI; the planner, the subagent that settles the kind, hands Pin the design's points and reads the design out for the generator; the pinner, Pin's subagent; the guard, Lane's check script laid into Turn; a round, one making of the work and its check; the content phase and the reading phase. It names Lane and Pin, and no plugin that calls Turn.

decisions.what: How does Turn deliver its UX, as one idea?
decisions.decided: Turn runs every kind of work by one course of subagents that Lane's routes move from one to the next. The planner settles the kind and hands Pin the work's goal, the kind's questions and the points the calling AI settled. Pin's pinner settles the design with the person, one point at a time. The generator makes the work from the design against the kind's best practice. The evaluator, fresh each round and never given the design, answers each question as the work's user would. A question not met goes back to its decision through Pin. Then the same two round again with the questions of how the work reads. up carries each point to the starter and each answer back as given. The opening links the UX for what this gives.

decisions.what: Who runs the course, and where does it run?
decisions.decided: up, Turn's own subagent turn:up, always in the background, for the person too. Lane's routes give it each next start from the result the last role gave. It reads and writes no file and decides nothing of the work. Why it beat an orchestrator in the main conversation: Lane checks only subagents, so only a subagent's course is held. The cost: each point passes two carriers, up and the starter, and a resume of up (KR1.2); the main conversation's passing is held by its steps alone; Turn runs only in an interactive session. Departs from Where the orchestrator runs and The orchestrator holds the whole and decides.

decisions.what: How does Turn settle a work's design: by Pin as built, or by a role of its own?
decisions.decided: By Pin as built. Turn is Pin's maker AI. The planner hands over in the design file: the work's goal where it is given, the kind's questions word for word, and each point the calling AI settled. up is Pin's go-between: it starts pin:pinner in the background as one of Turn's routed roles, puts each of its points to the starter as given, and resumes it with the answer word for word. Pin's own guard holds the pinner. A point the work raises goes back to Pin in a new Request, never into the design file by Turn. Why it beat a Turn role that follows the pinner's steps: Pin then runs as built and tested, held by its own rules, and no Turn file copies Pin's rules or steps. The cost: Lane must let a route name a dependency's subagent and keep its results, and Pin's pinner must give one result while a point waits and another once the design is confirmed.

decisions.what: Who settles the kind, and who stands between Turn's run and Pin?
decisions.decided: The planner, Turn's subagent turn:planner, on both sides of Pin. It settles the kind from given.kind or the request's words, and asks the person only where they leave it open. It finds the kind's best practice. It hands Pin the hand-over, and later each point the work raised. Once Pin hands the design back, it reads out where the work lies and what its user runs, for the generator. At the end it hands the work back. Why one role on both sides: one role alone decides what Turn hands Pin and what it takes from the design, and up stays a carrier. The cost: a run of the planner each time the design is handed over or comes back (KR1.2).

decisions.what: How does a kind new to Turn get its best practice?
decisions.decided: As a work of its own, made first in the same run by the same course, with meta as its best practice. Its design's goal is the purpose of such works, and its decisions hold the kind's parts and questions, so the person approves them when they approve that design. The generator writes it into .turn/best-practices/<kind>.json, where later runs in the repository find it. The planner then hands over the work itself. Why it beat a step of its own: one course for every kind, and the person approves the questions as they approve any design. The cost: the first work of a new kind takes a whole extra course, as the README says.

decisions.what: How do the generator and the evaluator work in rounds and phases?
decisions.decided: Two making roles only. The generator, one run per round, makes the whole work from the design against the best practice, answers every question of the round itself, and hands up the evaluator's runs. The evaluator runs once per group of the round's questions, at once, each fresh, with the work and the Standard alone. The phase is a value of the run: the content phase asks the kind's questions; the reading phase asks refactor-doc's or refactor-code's, by the same two roles. rounds.py alone decides each round's phase and questions from the run's files. Results: generator made or open; evaluator more, reword, met or good. Why one generator run per round beat one run per independent part: the first key result comes first, and parts made apart drift in voice and in what joins them. The cost: a work whose parts stand apart is made in order (KR1.2). Why several evaluator runs: each run is fresh on fewer questions, and they run at once (KR1.1, KR1.2); the cost is that each reads the whole work.
grounds: the brief: "Turn has two making roles, generator and evaluator. The refactoring phase runs the same two with the refactoring best practice (refactor-doc or refactor-code), the phase a value of the run, so refactorer and proofreader go."

decisions.what: What does the evaluator get, and what does a question not met lead to?
decisions.decided: The evaluator gets the work and the Standard alone: the best practice's goal, parts and questions, without its ways of meeting them, and never the design or the generator's own answers. The guard holds it to read nothing else. A question not met, and a point the generator finds that the design leaves open, go to the planner, which hands them to Pin in a Request; the pinner takes each back to the decisions that serve its question and settles them again. In the reading phase, a question not met goes back to the generator, and a point that would change what the work says goes to Pin.

decisions.what: Which principles of the plugin best practice does Turn take, depart from or not take?
decisions.decided: Turn builds on every principle and on Development, with these differences. It departs from Where the orchestrator runs and from The orchestrator holds the whole and decides (D3). Under Messages, up and the starter carry each point, as only the main conversation can ask the person. Under A plugin that uses another, Turn starts Pin's pinner, not a skill of Pin, as Pin's orchestrator is that subagent. It does not take Learning from each run: no step of the UX follows the work handed back, and the run's folder keeps each round for whoever looks. It departs from Unit: prompts, as Tests says.

decisions.what: Which principles does Turn add, each with its rule and its reason?
decisions.decided: Nine. One course for every kind (no role names a kind; KR1.1, KR1.2). Pin alone settles the design (no Turn role writes the design file after the hand-over or asks a point of it; KR1.1, KR2.1). The evaluator has only what the work's user has (KR1.1). A shortfall goes back to its decision (no fix beside the design; KR1.1). What the work says before how it says it (KR1.2). Each role starts fresh from the run's folder (KR1.1, KR1.2). Passed on as given (up and the planner change no point, answer or settled point; KR2.1, KR1.1). Turn knows no calling AI (no line names one; KR2.1). Turn changes only the work (no commit, push or write outside the work and the run's folder; commands only in a throwaway home; KR1.1). Four of them state an absence.

decisions.what: Do two developers of different parts reach the same decision on a case no rule names?
decisions.decided: Tried on an evaluator that sees a wrong option name in the work. The developer of the evaluator writes it as a question not met, with what the user lacks, and the developer of the generator does not mend it until it comes back through the design: A shortfall goes back to its decision says a fix beside the design is lost at the next round. Tried on a calling AI that gives a kind Turn lacks, with the work's goal. The developer of the planner hands over the best practice first with its goal open, and keeps the given goal for the work's hand-over: Passed on as given and One course for every kind both say so. The reason of Pin alone settles the design was sharpened to name a point the work raises.

decisions.what: Which user stories carry the UX's steps?
decisions.decided: S1: the person types /turn:up with a request and gets the first point that is theirs (O1: the request, and the first point put). S2: the person answers the point put to them and gets the next point, the design to approve, or the work (the rest of O1). S3: the calling AI starts turn:up with the request and what it settled, and gets the first point for the person (O2: the hand-over, its points kept). S4: the calling AI resumes turn:up with the person's answer word for word, and gets the next point, the design, or the work where it said (the rest of O2). S5: the person types /turn:up with a run's folder, alone or with a change (off the main path: KR1.2 for a stopped run, KR1.1 for a change taken in through the design). The person's own words to the calling AI in O2 lie outside Turn.

decisions.what: Which roles and stores are there, each with its type and technology?
decisions.decided: Roles of Turn: the main conversation [AI · Claude Code, by /turn:up's steps in Markdown]; up, planner, generator, evaluator [subagent · Claude Code, steps in Markdown]; the guard [hook script · Lane's code, Python 3.9]; Turn's scripts [command line · Python 3.9]: plan.py, rounds.py, throwaway.py. Stores: the run's folder [folder · JSON files: Design file, Run, Standard, Round, Answers]; best practices [files · JSON]; the work [the repository's files]; Rules laid [file · JSON]. Outside Turn: the person [person]; the calling AI [AI · Claude Code]; the pinner [Pin's subagent · Claude Code, held by Pin's guard]. The starter is drawn as one role: the steps that the main conversation or the calling AI follows, as Pin draws its go-between. Public pages appear in Deployment. An SVG with a legend.

decisions.what: Which arrows does the components figure draw?
decisions.decided: In the order they act: the person types /turn:up and answers (Call, Answer); the main conversation or the calling AI starts up and resumes it [Agent, SendMessage] (Call, Answer); the guard reads Rules laid and tells up each next start [Claude Code hooks] (Result); up starts each role in the background and resumes one that asked [Agent, SendMessage] (Run values, Request, Answer); the planner reads the best practice, has plan.py write the hand-over and the Standard, writes Run, and reads the design back; the pinner writes each point (Design file) and reads facts; the generator reads the design and the best practice, writes the work and its Answers; the evaluator reads the work whole and the Standard, and writes its Answers; generator and evaluator run rounds.py and throwaway.py; each role gives its Result and the guard checks each call; up ends with each Message; the main conversation puts it to the person.
grounds: architecture.json Q3 Practice step: "Draw an arrow for each thing one role asks of another, labelled with what it does and the data it hands on, not with a word such as \"uses\"."

decisions.what: Which role alone decides each point the stories need?
decisions.decided: The main conversation: nothing of the work; it carries. up: the run's folder, from given.run, a folder the request names, or a new one; and whom to resume with an answer. The planner: the kind, the best practice, the hand-over, what each Request to Pin carries, where the work lies and what its user runs, and when the run is done. The pinner: everything in the design. The generator: the work, and the small points of making it. The evaluator: whether each question of its group is met. plan.py: whether a best practice holds its form, the Standard and the hand-over's questions. rounds.py: each round's phase and questions, the evaluator's runs, and whether Answers hold. throwaway.py: where a work's command runs. The guard: whether a call or an end keeps its rules, and the next start.
grounds: architecture.json Q3 Practice step: "With the figure, write what each role alone decides that no arrow shows."

decisions.what: Does every story, role and data reach an objective?
decisions.decided: Each story names its UX steps or key result. Every role and data is reached by S2 or S4, the round of making; the planner's kind question only by S1 and S3. Gone, as no step or key result needs them: the designer, as Pin settles the design; the refactorer and the proofreader, as the phase is a value of the run; the researcher, as the pinner and the generator find facts themselves; the work's parts and the Remake, as one generator run makes the whole work; starts.py and tree.py, folded into rounds.py and plan.py. Kept off the main path: the stopped run and the change (S5), and the new kind's best practice (O1's opt step).
grounds: architecture.json Q7 Practice step: "Trace each role and each data to the stories whose sequences reach it. [...] Remove what reaches none."

decisions.what: Which data does the data model draw, and how do they join?
decisions.decided: Sixteen data by name, as an SVG: Call, Run, Work, Best practice, Question, Standard, Design file, Decision, Request, Run values, Round, Answers, Result, Rules laid, Message, Answer. Relations: a Call names one Run; a Run makes one or two Works in order; a Work is made by one Best practice and read by one more; a Best practice asks one or more Questions; a Standard is taken from one Best practice; a Work is designed in one Design file, which asks each Question and holds Decisions serving them; a Request names one Design file and carries the shortfalls of zero or more Answers; Run values start one run of a role on one Run; a Round checks one Work, with one or more Answers; an Answers answers each Question of its Round; a Message puts a point or names the Work; an Answer answers one Message; Rules laid route on Results. The fields lie where each data is built; one line under the figure says what each is.
grounds: architecture.json Q5 Practice step: "For each relation, ask whether the role that writes it and the role that reads it would keep it the same way."

decisions.what: Which sequences are drawn, and how?
decisions.decided: Three Mermaid sequences, as stories pair by who carries: the start (S1, S3, and S5 as a branch), up to the first point for the person; an answer (S2, S4) up to the next point or the design confirmed; the rounds (S2, S4 after the design is confirmed) up to the work handed back, with each send-back and the new kind's turn to the work. Participants named as in Components; data in brackets as in the data model; no semicolon in a message. Every step runs along an arrow of Components.
grounds: architecture.json Q6 Practice step: "Check that each step runs along an arrow of Components."

decisions.what: What are the routes?
decisions.decided: up to planner. planner: asks (no next start; a point waits), handed (pin:pinner), ready (generator), done (no next start; the work handed back). pin:pinner: asks (no next start), done (planner). generator: made (evaluator, in fan_out), open (planner). evaluator: more (planner), reword (generator), met (generator), good (planner). Order of results for the evaluator's runs: more, reword, met, good. A Markdown table looked up by row.

decisions.what: Which choices would a developer question, where do they stand, and what does each cost?
decisions.decided: Beside Components: up always a subagent; Pin used as built; the planner on both sides of Pin; one generator run per round; evaluator runs by groups; the new kind as a work by meta; the role before a step hands up its runs; no role starts a subagent. Beside the sequences: a role that asks gives asks, whose route starts no one; rounds.py settles the phase from the run's folder. Beside Deployment: commands in a throwaway home; the best practices of a new kind in .turn/best-practices/. Beside the tests: no unit trial of a prompt, and the weights. Each with why it beat the other way and its cost.
grounds: architecture.json Q15 Practice step: "check that each choice they would question has its reason and its cost beside it."

decisions.what: What leaves the document, as it holds how a role works inside?
decisions.decided: Out: each role's steps and wording, the lanes' sentences, the keys of each file, the subcommands of the scripts, the names of files inside a run's folder but design-tree.json and verification/, which the README promises, the form of the five lines a decision is put in, and how rounds.py groups questions. Kept: the result words, as the routes and the roles share them; the headings of a Message, by a link to calling.md. Checked by two changes: rounds.py grouping questions by part instead of by the whole, and the generator answering its own questions in another file; no line becomes untrue.

decisions.what: Where does each role run and each data lie, and how does Turn start?
decisions.decided: One environment, the person's computer: the Claude Code process [Claude Code 2.1.317 or later, interactive] with the main conversation or the calling AI, up, the planner, the generator, the evaluator and Pin's pinner; hook processes [python3 3.9 or later] with Turn's guard and Pin's; script processes [python3 3.9 or later] with Turn's scripts and each work's command in its throwaway home; installed Turn with Rules laid and Turn's best practices; installed Pin; the repository with the work, the run's folder and .turn/best-practices/; the temporary folder with Lane's kept calls and the throwaway homes. Outside: Anthropic's API; public pages the generator reads for a new kind; the marketplace. Start: install Turn, which installs Pin; type /turn:up, or a calling AI starts turn:up. An SVG.

decisions.what: Where do the files of each role and data lie?
decisions.decided: A tree, one line for each role and data: skills/up/SKILL.md (the main conversation's steps); agents/<role>.md and core/roles/<role>.md for up, planner, generator, evaluator; core/domain/best-practices/ (Best practice, Turn's); core/domain/forms/ (the form of Run, Run values, Round, Answers, Standard); core/domain/ modules and scripts/ for plan.py, rounds.py, throwaway.py; hooks/hooks.json, hooks/lanes.json (Rules laid), hooks/lane/ (the guard); docs/calling.md (the form of Call and Message); dev/turn/ with tests/unit, architecture, ux; .turn/<yyyymmdd>-<name>/ (Run, Design file, Standard) and its verification/ (Round, Answers); .turn/best-practices/ (Best practice, the repository's). Request and Answer to Pin take Pin's form, by a link.

decisions.what: Which levels test each deployment unit, how heavily, and which level is empty?
decisions.decided: A test table as an SVG, rows Turn's script processes, Turn's hook process and the Claude Code process. Scripts: unit ●●● unittest, coverage, Cosmic Ray, Hypothesis; architecture ●●● run real at each step; ux ●○○. Hook process: unit empty, as Lane's unit tests test the guard and Turn writes none of its code; architecture ●●● Turn's Rules laid run real on every path; ux ●○○. Claude Code process: unit empty, as no level tries a prompt alone; architecture ●●○ the entries as Claude Code takes them, every role a double; ux ●●○ trials on Opus. Left out: Pin's and Lane's units, each tested by its own plugin, run real in Turn's architecture tests where they join.
grounds: architecture.json Q11 Practice step: "Leave out a unit whose every cell would be empty, and say why under the table."
the brief: "ux trials (E2E on a subject big enough to bring out the frequent cases) find design faults and measure the variance by the key results."

decisions.what: What does each level run real, stand in with a double, cover, and pass on?
decisions.decided: Link the plugin best practice's Test; write what Turn adds. Unit: the classes of plan.py, rounds.py and throwaway.py, a decision table for the phase, and each script's three results. Architecture: Turn's scripts, Turn's guard on its Rules laid, Pin's check.py and the entries run real; doubles of up, the planner, the pinner, the generator, the evaluator, the starter, the person and Claude Code; one test per path of each sequence, in a Markdown table. Each double writes only files that the same check as the part's unit tests passes: Pin's check.py for the pinner's, rounds.py's for Answers, plan.py's for a best practice and a hand-over. ux: tidy at the size of a real request, run to bring out the frequent cases; an AI stand-in with an intent never shown to Turn; a plugin made for the test as the calling AI; 3 runs of 3; a measure for each key result, set against the last.
